narrative:
Your law school application was denied because the model estimated a 57.4% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is slightly more likely than passing, so the decision reflects a risk assessment, not a certainty about your ability.

The strongest factor behind the prediction was your first-year class standing: you were in the first decile, compared with an accepted average near the sixth, and this pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. The second most important factor was your undergraduate GPA of 3.40, which is above the accepted average of 3.23; this worked in your favor and pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the concerns about class standing. The third most important factor was your third-year class standing, at the second decile versus an accepted average near the sixth, which also pushed toward failure. Your lower-middle family income and full-time status were not among the top influences.

To improve future applications, seek academic advising and address the causes of your class-standing pattern, consider retaking the LSAT to strengthen your profile, gain legal or professional experience that demonstrates readiness, and discuss with admissions counselors whether a post-baccalaureate record, different program, or delayed application would be most useful.
